Lake Winnipeg south basin, Red River, Assiniboine River, Winnipeg River system, Whiteshell, Duck Mountain, Turtle Mountain areas fall in this division.

licensing: Who Needs A Licence: All persons, except those exempt, who engage in angling, dip netting, cast netting, seining, minnow trapping, spear fishing, and bow fishing must have a Manitoba Angling Licence on their person (printed or on an electronic device; must be shown to an officer on request). Licences are not transferable or refundable.

Fees 2026: GST added at time of purchase. Manitoba Resident (age 16-64): one-day $13.00, annual $28.00. Senior (age 65+): no licence required. Active military member or veteran (Manitoba resident): no licence required. Canadian Resident (age 16+): one-day $18.00, annual $43.00. Non-Canadian Resident (age 16+): one-day $26.00, annual $69.00.

Exemptions: Manitoba resident seniors 65+ (must show proof of age and Manitoba residency). Manitoba resident active military members and veterans (must show proof of Manitoba residency plus a Canadian Forces ID, Record of Service Card, or Veterans' Service Card). Manitoba resident youth under 16 with six months' permanent residence (own licence privileges and own limit). Status Indians do not require an angling licence. Canadian/non-Canadian resident youth under 16 must fish with a licence holder (or exempt person) and their catch counts toward that person's limit; they may buy their own licence to have their own limit.

Family Fishing Weekends: June 12-14, 2026 (summer) and February 20-22, 2027 (winter). During these weekends people may fish without an angling licence anywhere in Manitoba except federal (national) parks; all other rules still apply.

Border Waters: On waters crossing the Manitoba border, anglers may have only a Manitoba limit. On specified border lakes with Ontario (Davidson, Frances, Garner, High, Mantario, Moar, Ryerson lakes) either a Manitoba or Ontario licence suffices. On Lake of the Prairies upstream of Shellmouth Dam, either a Manitoba or Saskatchewan licence suffices.
National Parks: A Manitoba Angling Licence is not valid in national parks; a federal licence is required (Parks Canada).
general_rules: Barbless hooks are mandatory in Manitoba (hooks on all lines, in use or not, must be barbless).
Anglers may use only one rod and line, except during ice fishing when two may be used; only two hooks or lures per line.
Total fish length is measured from the most anterior part of the head to the most posterior part of the tail laid flat (not pinched); 2.54 cm = 1 inch.
Harvest, possession and use of live bait fish and leeches will be prohibited as of April 1, 2027.

Live bait fish currently may not be imported into Manitoba, and may not be used or possessed in the Northwest, North Central and Northeast Divisions (including the Bloodvein and Gammon rivers); in the Southern Division live bait is allowed in some areas with exceptions (stocked trout waters, Duck Mountain, Turtle Mountain, Porcupine Provincial Forest, Whiteshell, Winnipeg River from Seven Sisters Dam to the Ontario border, Atikaki/South Atikaki parks).

Ice fishing shelters must be removed by March 14, 2027 on the Red River, March 15 in Area B of the Southern Division, March 31 in the rest of the Southern Division, and April 15 in the Northwest/North Central/Northeast Divisions.
Catching and keeping fish during a species' closed season is prohibited (must not fish for the species during its closed season).

lakes.name: Lake Winnipeg
lakes.description: The 10th largest freshwater lake in the world, Lake Winnipeg is a shallow prairie lake (mean depth only 12 m) split into distinct north and south basins. It supports Manitoba's most famous walleye fishery - the iridescent greenback walleye - plus a major commercial fishery where walleye is the most important species. More than 50 fish species live in the lake.

lakes.name: Lake Manitoba
lakes.description: Canada's 14th largest lake, Lake Manitoba is a very shallow prairie lake about 75 km northwest of Winnipeg. It has supported a commercial fishery since 1895 and a long-standing recreational fishery for walleye, northern pike and yellow perch. Delta Marsh at its south end is one of North America's premier waterfowl staging areas.

lakes.name: Lake Winnipegosis
lakes.description: Manitoba's second-largest lake, Lake Winnipegosis is a shallow, turbid prairie lake west of Lake Winnipeg and north of Lake Manitoba. Its commercial fishery targets walleye, northern pike, lake whitefish and mullet species, while anglers pursue walleye and pike. Birch Island, at 806 km2, sits within the lake.

lakes.name: Lake of the Woods (Manitoba portion)
lakes.description: A vast multi-jurisdictional lake spanning Ontario, Manitoba and Minnesota, Lake of the Woods is one of North America's top multi-species fisheries. Manitoba's share lies in the lake's northwest reaches, reached via the Whiteshell-Kenora corridor. Anglers target walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike and muskie, with lake trout in deep areas like Clearwater Bay.

lakes.name: Lake Athapapuskow
lakes.description: A Canadian Shield lake near Flin Flon made of three connected basins - Big Athapap, Little Athapap and the North Arm - with depths ranging from shallow flats to basins over 200 feet. It is a trophy multi-species fishery famous for lake trout, with three historical world records including a 62 lb laker. Walleye, northern pike, rainbow trout, splake and smallmouth bass round out the fishery.

lakes.name: Clear Lake (Riding Mountain)
lakes.description: The showpiece lake of Riding Mountain National Park, Clear Lake is a moderately large, deep, spring-fed lake with exceptionally clear water. Parks Canada lists northern pike, yellow perch, walleye and lake whitefish as its prominent recreational species. The townsite of Wasagaming on its south shore is the park's commercial hub.

lakes.name: Falcon Lake
lakes.description: A popular Whiteshell Provincial Park lake about 152 km east of Winnipeg on the Trans-Canada Highway. Manitoba's 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye dominant at 79% of the survey catch, with northern pike, smallmouth and largemouth bass, yellow perch and lake whitefish also present. The lake is also famous for the 1967 Falcon Lake Incident UFO sighting.

lakes.name: West Hawk Lake
lakes.description: Formed by an ancient meteorite impact, West Hawk Lake is Manitoba's deepest lake with exceptionally clear water popular for scuba diving. The crater lake in Whiteshell Provincial Park holds walleye, northern pike, yellow perch and smallmouth bass; all trout must be released and trout fishing is closed Nov 1 to Apr 15. A Manitoba government bathymetric map is linked below.

lakes.name: Dauphin Lake
lakes.description: A shallow prairie lake east of the town of Dauphin, between Riding Mountain and Duck Mountain, with an average depth of only 2.35 m. Annual index netting shows walleye as the dominant species, with northern pike, yellow perch, suckers and bullheads. It drains via the Mossy River into Lake Winnipegosis.

lakes.name: Cedar Lake
lakes.description: A large, shallow lake on the Saskatchewan River system in north-central Manitoba. It is an important commercial fishery for walleye and lake whitefish. The town of Grand Rapids sits at its north end, where the Saskatchewan River continues toward Lake Winnipeg.

lakes.name: Kississing Lake
lakes.description: A northern Manitoba fly-in lake reached by floatplane from Flin Flon, home to the five-star Kississing Lake Lodge and the drive-to Kenanow Lodge. It offers trophy northern pike, walleye and lake trout, with anglers reporting up to 100-fish days. Whitefish and perch are also present year-round.

lakes.name: Reed Lake
lakes.description: The largest lake in Grass River Provincial Park, Reed Lake is known for intricate shoreline, islands and fish that grow to enormous size regardless of species. Anglers target walleye, lake trout, northern pike, burbot, perch, whitefish and tullibee. Special regulations limit walleye and pike harvest in the lake and its tributaries.

lakes.name: Gods Lake
lakes.description: Manitoba's seventh-largest lake, a deep, cold northern lake 344 miles north of Winnipeg. Elk Island Lodge operates fly-in trips for trophy northern pike, walleye, lake trout and brook trout. The lake is renowned for world-class catch-and-release trophy fishing.

lakes.name: Nueltin Lake
lakes.description: A vast subarctic lake of about 2,849 km2 total area, roughly 80% of it in Nunavut, on the Manitoba-Nunavut border. Partly protected by Nueltin Lake Provincial Park, it is accessible only by air and fished by fly-in lodges for trophy lake trout, northern pike and arctic grayling. Lake whitefish are also common.

lakes.name: Big Sand Lake
lakes.description: A remote fly-in lake in the Seal River system of far northern Manitoba, 550 miles north of Winnipeg. Big Sand Lake Lodge - the only lodge on the lake's roughly 60,000 acres of water - offers the Canadian Grand Slam: northern pike, lake trout, walleye and arctic grayling, all strict catch-and-release.

lakes.name: Wekusko Lake
lakes.description: A star-shaped lake in north-central Manitoba at the outlet of scenic Wekusko Falls, fished from Wekusko Falls Lodge. It produces thick-bodied chunky walleyes plus lake trout, northern pike, burbot, perch, whitefish and tullibee. Anglers can fish both Wekusko and nearby Reed Lake from the lodge.

lakes.name: Lake St. Martin
lakes.description: A lake in Manitoba's Interlake region between Lake Manitoba and Lake Winnipeg, connected to both via the Fairford and Dauphin rivers. Anglers report walleye, northern pike and freshwater drum. New outlet channels now help regulate its historically flood-prone water levels.

lakes.name: Cross Lake
lakes.description: A 755 km2 lake on the Nelson River in north-central Manitoba, scientifically studied for the effects of hydroelectric regulation on its fishery. Research documented lake whitefish, walleye, northern pike and cisco populations. It sits downstream of Lake Winnipeg on the Nelson River system.

lakes.name: Setting Lake
lakes.description: A northern Manitoba lake near Thompson listed among the province's notable drive-to walleye waters. It lies in the nickel-belt lake country of the Thompson area. Walleye are the main draw for visiting anglers.

lakes.name: Paint Lake
lakes.description: A large, clear Canadian Shield lake just south of Thompson in Paint Lake Provincial Park, renowned for dense populations of thick-bodied walleyes. Northern pike are also abundant. Paint Lake Lodge on its shore offers cabins, a full-service restaurant and boat rentals.

lakes.name: Laurie Lake
lakes.description: Part of the Laurie River system near Lynn Lake in northwest Manitoba, fished via Laurie River Lodge. The slow-flowing river system produces northern pike, walleye and lake trout, making it a true multi-species fly-in destination. It flows toward the Churchill River.

lakes.name: Gunisao Lake
lakes.description: A trophy walleye factory in northeastern Manitoba fished by Budd's Gunisao Lake Lodge. In 2022, 65% of all Manitoba Master Angler walleyes (May-August) were caught at Gunisao, with 708 Master Angler walleyes recorded. Trophy northern pike, whitefish, suckers and perch are also caught.

lakes.name: Clearwater Lake
lakes.description: A deep, clear, cold spring-fed lake in Clearwater Lake Provincial Park near The Pas, renowned for its excellent water quality and large lake trout. The nearly circular lake is 16 km across with a maximum depth of 39 m. Cold year-round temperatures slow trout growth but are essential for their survival.

lakes.name: Lake of the Prairies
lakes.description: A large reservoir on the Assiniboine River west of Roblin, with about 40 km of its length in Manitoba, developed with Asessippi Provincial Park, cottages and campgrounds. Index netting shows walleye dominant, with yellow perch, stocked muskellunge and smallmouth bass, plus carp, redhorse, mooneye, rock bass and quillback.

lakes.name: Schist Lake
lakes.description: A lake at Flin Flon in northwest Manitoba, bordered by Bakers Narrows Provincial Park. Area anglers pursue northern pike, walleye, lake trout and perch in open water and through the ice. It is part of the Flin Flon area's network of Shield lakes.

lakes.name: Crowduck Lake
lakes.description: A Whiteshell Provincial Park lake assessed by Manitoba Fisheries in 2023, holding walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, yellow perch, cisco and white suckers. Surveyed walleye averaged 46.8 cm, with fish up to 21 years old. It falls under the eastern region's special walleye regulation protecting fish over 45 cm.

lakes.name: High Lake
lakes.description: A backcountry lake near Falcon Lake in Whiteshell Provincial Park, reachable by portage from High Lake Bay at Falcon Lake's east end. This 8.0 km2 lake (max depth 30 m) holds self-sustaining lake trout plus lake whitefish, northern pike, burbot, white suckers and yellow perch. Trophy-class lake trout and whitefish have been documented.

lakes.name: Big Whiteshell Lake
lakes.description: A Whiteshell Provincial Park lake near the Ontario border in eastern Manitoba. Anglers most commonly report northern pike, walleye and yellow perch. It sits in the same Canadian Shield lake country as Falcon and West Hawk lakes.

lodges.name: Bakers Narrows Lodge
lodges.location: Bakers Narrows, Lake Athapapuskow (near Flin Flon)
lodges.description: Family-run, drive-to lodge on the shore of Lake Athapapuskow, about half a mile from the Flin Flon airport, with modern log cottages and guided fishing packages. The lake is known for producing some of Manitoba's largest lake trout, plus golden walleye and northern pike.

lodges.name: Kississing Lake Lodge
lodges.description: Fly-in fishing lodge reached by a 25-minute floatplane ride from Flin Flon, open May through September with private cabins and guided fishing. The lake is managed for trophy-size walleye, northern pike, and lake trout.

lodges.name: Blackwater Cats Outfitter
lodges.location: Selkirk / Lockport / Winnipeg (Red River and Lake Winnipeg)
lodges.description: Fully licensed and insured four-season guide service based in Winnipeg and operating out of Lockport, Selkirk, and Hecla Island. Specializes in giant Red River channel catfish and trophy greenback walleye on the Winnipeg River, Red River, and south basin of Lake Winnipeg, including winter ice fishing.

lodges.name: Cat Eye Outfitter
lodges.location: Selkirk (Red River, Winnipeg River, Lake Winnipeg)
lodges.description: Guided fishing service led by Dan Kiazyk, operating year-round on the Red River, Winnipeg River, and Lake Winnipeg. Specializes in trophy channel catfish and greenback walleye, with all bait and equipment supplied.

lodges.name: CatDaddy Fishing Guide Service
lodges.description: Fully licensed fishing outfitter based in Selkirk, led by guide Paul Munroe. Specializes in trophy channel catfish on the Red River and also fishes walleye on Lake Winnipeg, Traverse Bay, and Lake of the Woods, with all boats, tackle, and bait supplied.

lodges.name: City Cats Guiding Service
lodges.description: Guiding service operating since 1999, specializing in monster channel catfish trips on the Red River from May through September. Also runs fall greenback walleye tours on the Red River and winter ice fishing trips for walleye on Lake Winnipeg.

lodges.name: Big Sand Lake Lodge
lodges.description: Fly-in lodge about 550 miles north of Winnipeg, the only lodge on a 60,000-acre lake in the Seal River system. Packages include the round-trip flight from Winnipeg and guided fishing for lake trout, northern pike, walleye, and arctic grayling, with four outpost camps on additional lakes.

lodges.name: Nueltin Fly-In Lodges
lodges.description: Fly-in lodge operation on Nueltin Lake in northern Manitoba, also serving Kasmere Lake and Shannon Lake, with a pioneer catch-and-release program. Targets trophy northern pike, lake trout, and arctic grayling in remote subarctic waters.

lodges.name: Elk Island Lodge
lodges.description: Family-run fly-in fishing lodge on God's Lake in northeastern Manitoba, about 344 miles north of Winnipeg. Guests fish for walleye, northern pike, lake trout, and brook trout with modern boats and experienced guides, plus fly-out brook trout trips on the Gods River.

lodges.name: Healey's God's Lake Narrows Lodge
lodges.description: Working wilderness lodge at Gods Lake Narrows, known for world-class lake trout fishing; Manitoba's all-time record lake trout was certified here in 1998. Offers guided fishing in 18-foot Lund boats across 65 miles of clear water dotted with islands.

lodges.name: Trail End Camp & Outfitters
lodges.location: Pointe du Bois (Winnipeg River, north end of Whiteshell Provincial Park)
lodges.description: Drive-to, four-season lodge on the Winnipeg River run by Vance and Maureen Hrechkosy, with full-service waterfront cabins, rental boats, guides, and a charter boat service. The river holds walleye, northern pike, perch, sturgeon, and smallmouth bass, and the camp offers ice fishing packages in winter.

lodges.name: Webber's Lodges
lodges.location: North Knife Lake and Dymond Lake (fly-in)
lodges.description: Fly-in fishing operator with North Knife Lake Lodge and Dymond Lake Lodge in northern Manitoba, run on a strict catch-and-release policy. Targets lake trout, northern pike, and arctic grayling in remote subarctic lakes.

lodges.name: Kannuk Outfitters
lodges.description: Professional guide service offering all-inclusive guided ice fishing trips on Lake Winnipeg, chasing the schools of greenback walleye in the south basin. Trips include a professional guide, pop-up ice shacks, bait, propane heaters, lunch, rods, tackle, and flashers; luxury Ice Castle fish house rentals are also offered.

lodges.name: Lake Winnipeg Ice Fishing Shack Rentals
lodges.location: Balsam Harbour, east side of Lake Winnipeg
lodges.description: Ice shack rental operator on the east side of Lake Winnipeg at Balsam Harbour. Shacks sleep 4-6 people, are fully insulated and heated, and holes are drilled for guests each day; walleye is the primary target.

lodges.name: Laurie River Lodge
lodges.description: Fly-in lodge on McGavock Lake near Lynn Lake, reached via charter flights from Winnipeg and floatplane from Lynn Lake. Offers both guided all-inclusive packages and do-it-yourself outpost trips across about 1,600 square miles of wilderness, targeting trophy walleye, northern pike, and lake trout.

lodges.name: North Haven Resort
lodges.description: Fly-in fishing resort on Utik Lake in north-central Manitoba, the only lodge on the lake. Offers guided fishing for trophy northern pike, walleye, and lake trout with private lakefront cabins, fine dining, and spa facilities.

lodges.name: Aikens Lake Wilderness Lodge
lodges.description: Fly-in fishing lodge established in 1949 inside Atikaki Provincial Park in Manitoba's Eastern Region, reached only by floatplane. Set on a sandy beach near the Gammon River inlet, it targets trophy walleye, northern pike, and lake trout with a main lodge, mini-lodge, and outpost options.

lodges.name: Moak Lodge and Campground
lodges.location: Cross Bay, Cedar Lake (near Grand Rapids, drive-to)
lodges.description: Drive-to lodge on Cross Bay of Cedar Lake, 450 km north of Winnipeg near Grand Rapids, with cabin rentals, rental boats, and tent/RV camping. Targets trophy northern pike, walleye, burbot, and stocked rainbow trout, and takes ice fishing reservations through March and April.

lodges.name: Icebound Excursions
lodges.description: SnoBear ice fishing outfitter on Lake Winnipeg, offering self-drive SnoBear rentals and guided SnoBear excursions since 2017. Primary target is the lake's famous greenback walleye, with northern pike and black crappie also possible.

lodges.name: Bruin Outfitting
lodges.location: Lake Winnipeg (SnoBear ice fishing); Lake of the Woods (open-water musky)
lodges.description: Guided fishing charter founded in 2004 by Matt Cornell, offering SnoBear and run-and-gun ice fishing trips for greenback walleye on Lake Winnipeg. In open water the operation also runs musky fishing trips on Lake of the Woods.

lodges.name: Evergreen Lodge and Resort
lodges.description: Drive-in resort near The Pas with a main lodge, lakefront cabins, and an outpost camp, run by hosts Ken and Faye Kobelka. Offers guided ice fishing trips on Clearwater Lake in winter, where ice fishing for lake trout, northern pike, whitefish, and burbot is popular.

best_spots.name: South basin (Balsam Harbour / Balsam Bay)
best_spots.description: The province's marquee ice fishery; guides and hut operators work out of access points on both the east and west sides to follow roaming walleye schools.

best_spots.name: Mouth of the Red River
best_spots.description: Greenback walleye gather where the Red River enters the south basin; SnoBear outfitters run east across the lake to this area.

best_spots.name: St. Andrews Lock and Dam
best_spots.description: The Lockport Ice Fishing Village offers easy river access, icehouse rentals (including the 'Cat House' and 'Taj Mahal'), and winter walleye fishing; summer brings catfish.

best_spots.name: Pine Falls to Traverse Bay
best_spots.description: Blackwater Cats guides ice fishing on the Winnipeg River as well as the Red River and Lake Winnipeg, targeting greenback walleye.

best_spots.name: Cross Bay
best_spots.description: Drive-to fishery near Grand Rapids with trophy walleye, pike, burbot, and stocked rainbow trout; Moak Lodge takes ice fishing reservations March through April.

best_spots.name: Bakers Narrows
best_spots.description: Short snowmobile rides from Bakers Narrows Lodge reach waters known for some of Manitoba's largest lake trout, plus golden walleye and northern pike.

best_spots.name: Near Flin Flon
best_spots.description: Stocked trout lake close to Moak Lodge; winter fishing for rainbow, tiger, brown, and brook trout.

best_spots.name: Near Roblin
best_spots.description: DIY-friendly stocked lake off Highway 83, close to shore access, known for energetic tiger trout.

best_spots.name: The Pas area
best_spots.description: Provincial park waters where winter ice fishing for lake trout, northern pike, whitefish, and burbot is popular; Evergreen Lodge and Resort offers guided trips and cabins.

best_spots.name: Interlake region
best_spots.description: Year-round drive-to fishing in the Interlake region between Lakes Winnipeg and Manitoba; signature species include greenback walleye and yellow perch.

hut_rentals.lake: Balsam Harbour, east side of Lake Winnipeg

safety:
Manitoba is one of Canada's top ice fishing destinations, with a long winter season and thousands of lakes offering hardwater fishing from December through March. The signature target is the greenback walleye of Lake Winnipeg's south basin — a uniquely colored strain of walleye that draws trophy hunters from across North America — but the province's ice fisheries are far more diverse than one lake. Stocked trout lakes such as Foot Print Lake and Twin Lake produce rainbow, tiger, brown, and brook trout, while northern drive-to lakes like Cedar Lake and Lake Athapapuskow give up walleye, northern pike, lake trout, and burbot.

Access ranges from fully guided day trips to remote lodge stays. SnoBear outfitters on Lake Winnipeg rent heated, self-drive mobile ice shacks or run guided excursions that chase roaming walleye schools, and guides on the Red River put anglers on winter walleye at Lockport and trophy channel catfish through the ice. Lodges such as Bakers Narrows Lodge on Lake Athapapuskow, Moak Lodge on Cedar Lake, and Evergreen Lodge and Resort near The Pas host multi-day ice fishing stays, while experienced anglers can drive to DIY-friendly waters like Twin Lake near Roblin. Outfitters generally supply heated shelters, augers, rods, tackle, and local knowledge, making the sport accessible to first-timers as well as seasoned hardwater anglers.

Safety comes first: Manitoba ice conditions change fast, and checking local ice reports is essential before heading out. Provincial fishing regulations — including seasons, slot limits, and licence requirements — apply on the ice exactly as they do in open water, so review the current Manitoba Angler's Guide before you fish.

Only go on ice at least 10 cm (4 in) thick for ice fishing on foot, 14 cm (5.5 in) for a snowmobile or ATV, and 32 cm (12.5 in) or more for a car or small truck. These minimums assume new, clear, solid ice — double the thickness for white or snow ice.

Ice seldom freezes uniformly; it can be 30 cm thick in one spot and 10 cm a few metres away. Test thickness repeatedly with a spud bar or auger as you move, especially after traveling across cracks or pressure ridges.
Stay away from river inlets and outlets, streams, culverts, and bridge pilings — moving water is the last to freeze and the first to thaw, and ice there is often dangerously thin.
Never venture onto the ice alone; a slip, fall, or breakthrough can be fatal without help nearby.
Before every trip, check local ice thickness reports and follow Manitoba provincial fishing regulations, including season dates and limits.
Tell someone where you are going and when you expect to return, and carry ice picks, a rope, and a charged phone in a waterproof bag.

species_advice.overview: Manitoba's signature sport fish. Lake Winnipeg's famous green-backed walleye draw ice anglers from around the world, while the Red River offers a strong fall run near Lockport.
techniques: Jigging live minnows near bottom on structure
Trolling crankbaits along contours in open water
Drifting with bottom bouncers and nightcrawlers
Ice fishing with rattle baits and jigging spoons
Deadstick rod with live bait next to an active jigging rod
species_advice.best_seasons: Spring and fall open water; September-October fall run on the Red River; prime ice fishing December through March.

species_advice.overview: Manitoba's aggressive ambush predator, found in everything from Lake Winnipeg's bays to remote northern fly-in lakes, with true trophy potential.
techniques: Casting spoons, spinnerbaits and jerkbaits along weed edges and rocky points
Fly fishing with large streamers and poppers on an 8-weight rod
Ice fishing with tip-ups baited with large shiners or sucker minnows
Trolling to cover water and locate active fish
baits: Large shiners or sucker minnows on tip-ups
species_advice.best_seasons: Spring, when pike pack into warming bays and river mouths; steady summer action on weedlines; fall for trophy fish on points and windblown shorelines; winter ice season with tip-ups.

species_advice.overview: Deep, cold shield lakes in northern Manitoba — Lake Athapapuskow, Clearwater, the Cranberry Chain, Wekusko and Kississing — hold some of the biggest lake trout anywhere, and they're very catchable through the ice.
techniques: Jigging heavy tubes, jigs and spoons on deep structure
Dead sticking with ciscos on points or saddles
Trolling deep with downriggers or lead-core line in summer
Casting bucktail jigs in shallow water during spring and fall
species_advice.best_seasons: Winter through the ice; late August to early September when big females move onto shallow rocky reefs for the fall spawn; early spring when trout ride higher in the water column.

species_advice.overview: The Red River below the Lockport Dam is one of North America's premier trophy channel cat fisheries, with 20-plus-pound fish common and 30-pounders attainable.
techniques: Slip-sinker bottom rigging behind an anchored boat
Slip-bobber float fishing along current edges
Anchoring at the head or edge of holes and casting rigs downriver
species_advice.best_seasons: Late May-June prespawn bite in tailwaters is the peak; fishing stays strong through summer and into October.

species_advice.overview: Clear Canadian Shield lakes in Nopiming and Whiteshell Provincial Parks grow aggressive smallmouth that feed heavily on crayfish around rocks and boulders.
techniques: Casting tube jigs along rocky points and boulders
Drop shotting near deeper structure
Jerkbait retrieves along shorelines
Topwater walking baits early in the day
Finesse presentations on subtle points and corners
species_advice.best_seasons: Late spring through early fall; late fall can produce when fish school up.

species_advice.overview: Manitoba's Interlake shoal lakes produce jumbo perch, and Lake Winnipeg perch keep ice anglers busy all winter with fast, tasty action.
techniques: Jigging small tungsten jigs and spoons tipped with bait
Dead sticking with live minnows on ultra-light rods
Rattle baits when perch are aggressive
species_advice.best_seasons: Winter ice season, especially late ice in March when perch move shallow; summer jigging in deeper water.

species_advice.overview: Manitoba's freshwater cod is a winter specialty — Cedar Lake is famous for its burbot spawn under the ice, and the Red River's deeper stretches hold them too.
techniques: Night jigging with heavy glow spoons
Dead sticking with scented bait near bottom
Tip-ups rigged just off bottom overnight
species_advice.best_seasons: Winter, peaking around the March spawn under the ice.

species_advice.overview: An underrated ice-fishing target in Manitoba — Lake Winnipeg and Cedar Lake both hold trophy-class whitefish that reward a finesse approach.
techniques: Finesse jigging with compact spoons and jigs
Staying mobile to locate roaming schools
Light presentations that keep the lure above the fish

species_advice.overview: A Manitoba river classic — bright silver, eager biters in the Red, Assiniboine and Winnipeg Rivers, and the province's famous smoked fish delicacy.
techniques: Slip-bobber fishing with worms close to shore
Casting small spinners, spoons and jigs
species_advice.best_seasons: Spring and early summer as river water warms; active through the summer months.

species_advice.overview: Manitoba stocks rainbows in lakes like Footprint Lake and throughout the Whiteshell, giving shore and ice anglers fun, hard-fighting trout close to home.
techniques: Still fishing with a small jig and nightcrawler a foot or two off bottom
Casting small spoons and spinners
Fly fishing with streamers and leech patterns in fall
species_advice.best_seasons: Fall, when stocked trout feed aggressively on shallow weed flats; winter through the ice; spring after ice-out.

master_angler.about: The Manitoba Master Angler Program is a trophy-fish recognition program run by Travel Manitoba (with the Manitoba Wildlife Federation historically involved). Any angler who catches a fish in Manitoba meeting or exceeding the program's minimum length for one of 30 eligible species can register it. Awards are given per qualifying fish, with bronze/silver/gold/platinum/diamond milestone badges for number of different species caught, plus specialist badges per species, and special recognition for catch-and-release. Program website: anglers.travelmanitoba.com.
how_it_works: Catch a fish in Manitoba (in accordance with provincial angling regulations, using hook and line) that meets or exceeds the minimum length for its species.
Take a horizontal measurement photo of the entire length of the fish against a ruler, measuring tape or bump board (photo must meet rule #3; action photo optional but encouraged).
Submissions with images showing vertical gill/eye holds, weigh-scale or fish-stringer holds, frozen fish declared as released, thumbnails/screen captures, or blood in photos are not accepted.
Submit digitally through the Master Angler Awards website (anglers.travelmanitoba.com) or the Master Angler mobile app within one year of the catch.
Travel Manitoba is the sole and final judge of entries.

Every qualifying fish receives a certificate (digital certificate by email for non-level-achieving catches; mailed hard copy for the first Master Angler award and when a new level or specialist badge is achieved); catch-and-release catches earn a special release recognition/crest.

hot_lakes.report: Anglers posting on YouTube and social media in late September and early October 2026 report a strong fall greenback walleye bite off Hecla Island, with guided boats landing 40+ walleye in a day, multiple fish over 27 inches, and one guide boat reporting a 100-fish day with two Manitoba Master Angler walleye. Simple jigs with plastic or live bait near the Gull Harbour lighthouse are the pattern being shared.

hot_lakes.report: Posts from October 2026 describe productive fall fishing on the Red River near Lockport: a guided pontoon trip on Oct 6 landed multiple large channel catfish with the top fish earning a Manitoba Master Angler mention, and an Oct 1 trip report shows a mixed bag of northern pike, greenback walleye, bullhead catfish, and freshwater drum.

This is a guide marketing post, so treat it as a signal of fish being caught rather than an independent catch report.
